title: Quality benchmarking & drift detection walkthrough — Aurora Health

Agreed next steps: pilot baseline run, share SOC2 and network diagrams, and schedule a 2-week trial with a small prompt set.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-19 14:30 PDT | Duration: 68m | Recording: Fireflies
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Dana Lopez (Aurora Head of AI), Samir Patel (Platform), Julia Tran (Compliance)

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everybody, thanks for taking the time, we're excited to walk through our quality playbook today — prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B compares, how it ties into Console and Optimize.
[00:18] Dana: Thanks Ethan, quick context: Aurora is running a clinical triage assistant in prod on Vertex, latency's ok but we're seeing occasional regressions after model updates. We need tighter evals and guardrails, ideally with PHI-safe telemetry.
[00:35] Maya: Totally, that's exactly the use case Optimize was built for. We'll demo the prompt-set flow, then a live A/B compare and show the regression alerting on top. I'll flag the parts that require private deployment or VPC.
[00:52] Samir: Couple constraints up front: we can't forward PHI to third-party logs, and any keys must be KMS-managed. Also prefer SSO for shared access.
[01:06] Ethan: Got it. We support customer-managed KMS and SSO/SAML; we'll add the SOC2 and network diagram after.
[01:20] Julia: From compliance perspective, we need retention controls and proof of audit logs for any PHI redaction.
[01:29] Maya: A note — Optimize has a redaction-first ingestion mode and token-level cost view so you can map cost to failing prompts. We'll show an example.
[01:42] Ethan: Alright Maya, take it away.

[02:05] Maya: Opening Console — prompt-sets module. Here you can group prompts by intent, attach expected outputs or canonical labels, and run scheduled evaluations. You can also attach a baseline run that becomes the comparison point for regression alerts.
[02:28] Maya: Example: we've got a "triage_pain_level" prompt set. You can see per-prompt metrics — exact match, semantic similarity, BLEU-ish style scores, and custom scoring functions. Slight note: the transcript shows BLEU but internally we compute pairwise embeddings distance with micro-thresholds.
[02:52] Dana: How granular are thresholds? Can we get per-prompt sensitivity?
[02:59] Maya: Yep. You can tune sensitivity per-prompt and per-metric. There's a two-tier system: soft alerts (informational) and hard alerts that trigger rollback policies.
[03:15] Samir: Rollback? Meaning if a model update causes a hard alert, it can automatically route to previously pinned model?
[03:23] Maya: Exactly. You can pin the previous version and set an automatic fallback route in Smart Routing. It's configurable — you pick which traffic percentage to divert.

[03:40] Ethan: Quick product aside — this works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments so you can keep telemetry on-prem if needed.
[03:49] Dana: Ok show the A/B flow. We want to compare the baseline current model vs a proposed tuned variant.

[04:10] Maya: A/B compare: create two cohorts, assign prompts (or random sample), pick metrics, and run a pairwise comparison. Console shows pairwise diffs and a significance test. Note: significance uses bootstrapped samples; if you have small N we recommend pairwise preference labeling.
[04:36] Dana: Do you support blind human evals? We need clinician-blind scoring for certain prompts.
[04:42] Maya: Yes — you can create an export for human review UI. Labelers see prompt+response A/B and pick preference. Labels feed back into the dashboard and can raise regression alerts.

[05:02] Samir: On costs, what's the token accounting for A/B runs? If we run 2k prompts across two models, that's 4k model calls — do you charge hosted inference or is it included in pilot?
[05:18] Ethan: For pilots we usually provide a small allowance; normal pricing is per-token for hosted. For Dedicated we offer committed capacity. We'll put a pilot estimate in the follow-up.

[05:33] Maya: Now showing Optimize recommendations — for your triage workload we suggest mid-sequence quantization and a modest batch target to hit 100ms p95 while keeping cost down. There's a recommended profile which maps to a config you can push from Console to your deployment.
[05:55] Dana: How do you validate that the quantized model doesn't regress on critical prompts?
[06:02] Maya: We run pre/post evals with the exact prompt set, and we tie alerts to the delta. You can set thresholds that ignore <1% drop in semantic sim but flag >3% drop.

[06:20] Ethan: Real quick demo: kicking off a baseline run. I'll upload a handful of prompts (we'll use a contrived 30 for the demo) and run A/B between v1.2 (baseline) and v1.3-tuned.
[06:36] Maya: Transcript note: upload may lag, small stutter.
[06:44] [06:45] Maya: Upload complete. Starting evaluation — ETA ~8 minutes for 30 prompts across 2 models.
[07:03] Dana: While that runs, can you show the regression alerts UI?
[07:09] Maya: Sure. Alerts tab — you can create rules like "semantic_sim_drop > 3% for N consecutive runs". Alerts support paging to Slack, webhook, or an internal playbook that runs a canary rollback.
[07:28] Samir: Can webhooks include masked PHI? I assume not.
[07:35] Maya: Correct, payloads can be configured to strip or hash user text. We also support on-prem metrics ingestion if you need zero egress.

[07:46] [10:12] Maya: Quick pause — the run finished. Results are in.
[10:18] Maya: For this toy set, we show a handful of prompts where v1.3 is slightly better on semantic sim but worse on a clinical-entity extraction metric. Console surfaces the tradeoff and you can drill into per-example differences, see the two outputs side by side, and add tags (e.g., "regression-risk").
[10:44] Dana: That's great, seeing per-example diffs helps a lot. Is there an API to fetch the pairwise diffs programmatically?
[10:52] Maya: Yes — the Redwood API has endpoints for prompt-sets, runs, and per-item diffs; responses are JSON and you can pull them into your internal dashboards.
[11:03] Samir: If we do this in Private with a customer control plane, will the diff artifacts stay in-region?
[11:10] Ethan: Yes, in Private deployments data residency is enforced and artifacts are stored per your retention policy.

[11:22] Julia: Can you show an example of a false positive alert and how to tune it down?
[11:29] Maya: Example — an alert triggered because of a single outlier. You can configure cadence and min sample size and add noise-robust scoring like smoothed rolling-averages. There's also an ignore list for prompts known to be noisy.
[11:47] Dana: How do you handle concept drift over weeks vs sudden regression after deploy?
[11:54] Maya: We have two mechanisms: long-term drift detection using trend analysis on the metric time series, and short-term regression detection tied to discrete runs. For drift, you get an automated reminder to re-baseline and an option to automatically flag prompts that drift beyond a sliding window.

[12:12] [13:00] Ethan: A few questions from our side: what are your success metrics for the POC? How many prompts and what latency/cost SLOs?
[13:08] Dana: We want clinician-acceptable output on 95% of the core prompts, p95 latency < 200ms for single-turn triage, and an upper budget for inference costs. We'll share exact numbers in the doc.
[13:20] Ethan: Perfect. We'll size the pilot to those numbers.

[13:34] Samir: A slightly technical question — do you capture KV cache warm-start in the evals? Our live traffic benefits from hot KV caches and isolated evals can understate latency.
[13:44] Maya: Good call. You can simulate warmed KV cache in runs by setting a warmup sequence or using trace replay. Optimize also estimates steady-state latency vs cold-start.
[13:56] Dana: Any limitations on pairwise comparisons with human labels? We may need to run blinded clinicians across 5k cases.
[14:06] Maya: Scaling human evals is fine — we provide exports and a built-in reviewer UI; costs are extra for managed labeling but you can integrate your vendor. We'll include guidance in the pilot plan.

[14:30] Ethan: Competitor question: some customers ask if this is just a wrapper for OpenAI or Anthropic. Short answer: we support many model backends but the value is the runtime, auditability, and rollout controls.
[14:42] Dana: Understood. We also asked security on the pre-call form; please include encryption at rest and key rotation details.
[14:50] Ethan: Will do.

[15:07] Maya: Demo wrap — re-iterate pilot proposal: 2-week pilot, 2k prompts (or smaller canonical set), run baseline vs candidate, human blind eval on top 200, and set alerts to guard rails. We'll provide a cost estimate and a config YAML you can push.
[15:28] Dana: Sounds good. One more compliance question: can audit logs be forwarded into our SIEM?
[15:34] Ethan: Yes, logs can stream to your SIEM or we can provide S3 export with KMS encryption.

[15:45] Julia: Ok I'm satisfied for compliance, pending the docs.
[15:50] Dana: Thanks everyone, this was useful.

[16:03] Ethan: Recap: we'll send security docs, pilot config, and pricing. Maya will propose the pilot YAML and runbook. Dana to send prompts and metrics.

[16:20] Samir: Quick sidebar — if we need Private deployment, what's the typical lead time?
[16:27] Ethan: For standard VPC private it's ~4-6 weeks for network setup and validation; on-prem air-gapped can be longer. We'll include an options matrix in follow-up.

[16:42] Dana: Great, let's aim for kickoff week of 8/31.
[16:47] Ethan: Perfect, we'll follow up. Thanks all.

[16:55] Meeting end.
